 Onondaga County elections guide 2026 
 Central Current has prepared a paywall-free election guide to help inform you about the candidates and issues shaping each race. 
 by 
 Chris Libonati 
 October 23, 2026 October 23, 2026 
 Credit: Maddi Jane Brown | Central Current 
 We hope the guide below helps you stay informed about the people who want to represent you in local government. Along with the interviews, our guide includes information on voter registration and polling locations.
 Our newsroom publishes exclusively community-focused reporting that is independent and ad-free. Subscribe today to join us.
 Sign up 
 Explore the links below to access candidate Q&As along with analysis from our CNY Decides project — a collaboration with WAER Syracuse Public Media designed to demystify the political process and bring you the stories and information you’ll remember in the voting booth.

 Editor’s Note: Central Current has contacted all local candidates and their party leaders as part of our initiative to include Q&As for all local races. We are still awaiting responses from some candidates and will update this guide as those responses are received.

 Onondaga County Propositions
 An explanation of how these different term limit options would work can be found by clicking here . 
 Proposition 1: Establishing a term limit of three (3) consecutive four-year terms for the office of County Executive and the office of County Comptroller.
 Proposition 2: Establishing a term limit of four (4) consecutive four-year terms for the office of County Executive and the office of County Comptroller.
 Video: How Term Limits Became an Onondaga County Ballot Battle

 Dates, deadlines, and resources for the Nov. 3rd election
 Registration deadline: To be eligible to vote in the 2026 general election, your registration application must be submitted to the board of elections no later than October 24th, 2026.
 Early voting: Saturday, October 24th through Tuesday, November 1st, 2026.
 Election Day: Tuesday, November 3rd, 2026.
 You can check your registration status, polling location, access a sample ballot, and check your mail-in ballot status by visiting the New York State Board of Elections voter lookup page .
